paper_metadata.title: Superior cryogenic tensile properties of ultrafine-grained CoCrNi medium-entropy alloy produced by high-pressure torsion and annealing

evidence.quote: ultrafine-grained CoCrNi medium-entropy alloy with nanotwins is fabricated by high-pressure torsion followed by annealing; and investigated for cryogenic tensile properties.

phases_and_microstructures.name: FCC phase
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: UFG; HPT + annealed at 600 °C for 60 min

evidence.quote: The XRD pattern indicates (Fig. 1f) the presence of a single FCC phase.

phases_and_microstructures.name: ultrafine grain
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: UFG; HPT + annealed at 600 °C for 60 min

evidence.quote: with an average grain size of ~650 nm

phases_and_microstructures.name: annealing nanotwin
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: UFG; HPT + annealed at 600 °C for 60 min

evidence.quote: The TKD image (Fig. 1c) and STEM-BF (Fig. 1d) image show the presence of nanotwins in most of the grains.

phases_and_microstructures.name: sub-grain boundary
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: UFG; HPT + annealed at 600 °C for 60 min

evidence.quote: The STEM-BF image shows the presence of sub-grain boundaries (shown by a red arrow) and few residual dislocations (shown by a green arrow) within the grains.

phases_and_microstructures.name: residual dislocation
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: UFG; HPT + annealed at 600 °C for 60 min

evidence.quote: The presence of residual dislocations indicates the recovery of dislocations induced during HPT is not complete.

phases_and_microstructures.name: deformation twin
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: UFG; cryogenic tensile tested at 77 K (post-deformed)

evidence.quote: the post deformed microstructure shows very fine deformation twins/stacking faults (SFs) (Fig. 3a–d), subgrain boundaries (Fig. 3c), and high density of dislocations (Fig. 3c).

phases_and_microstructures.name: dislocation
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: UFG; cryogenic tensile tested at 77 K (post-deformed)

evidence.quote: the post deformed microstructure shows very fine deformation twins/stacking faults (SFs) (Fig. 3a–d), subgrain boundaries (Fig. 3c), and high density of dislocations (Fig. 3c).

evidence.quote: The UFG sample shows very high cryogenic yield (σy) and tensile strength (σUTS) of 1975 MPa and 2054 MPa, respectively.

mechanisms.name: grain-boundary strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: UFG; HPT + annealed at 600 °C for 60 min

evidence.quote: The high strength achieved in the present alloy at cryogenic temperature could be attributed to the fine grain size, annealing nanotwins, residual dislocation density in the initial material, and strong temperature dependence of yield strength.

mechanisms.name: twin-boundary strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: UFG; HPT + annealed at 600 °C for 60 min

evidence.quote: The strengthening from grain boundary and annealing nanotwins can be explained based on the Hall-Petch strengthening, which indicates the strength increases when the dislocation mean-free path decreases.

mechanisms.name: dislocation strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: UFG; HPT + annealed at 600 °C for 60 min

evidence.quote: The residual dislocation in the initial microstructure can contribute to strengthening by acting as a barrier to dislocation motion.

mechanisms.name: deformation twinning
mechanisms.material_state: UFG; cryogenic tensile tested at 77 K (post-deformed)

evidence.quote: The estimated twinning stress is lower than the tensile yield strength of UFG CoCrNi MEA. Thus, the deformation twinning is observed even in UFG CoCrNi MEA.

mechanisms.name: dislocation saturation
mechanisms.material_state: UFG; cryogenic tensile tested at 77 K (post-deformed)

evidence.quote: The dislocation saturation at very low strain could be due to the fine grain size and presence of residual dislocation in the initial material.

mechanisms.name: temperature dependence of yield strength
mechanisms.material_state: UFG; HPT + annealed at 600 °C for 60 min

evidence.quote: The high friction stress and its strong temperature dependence of yield strength can result in higher yield strength at cryogenic temperature than at room temperature.
